title: Stability canonicalization and seed heuristics for throughput benchmarking
summary: Working notes and a concise methodology for producing repeatable throughput numbers: canonical workload selection, seed hygiene, temporal stabilization heuristics and a minimal warmup cadence tailored to modern GPU inference runtimes.
body:
Purpose
This doc captures our pragmatic approach to reduce run-to-run throughput variance when benchmarking the serving runtime. It focuses on three levers we can control: canonicalization of the workload (inputs and arrival patterns), RNG/seed hygiene, and an explicit temporal stabilization (warmup + measurement trimming) heuristic. These notes are intentionally prescriptive so benchmark runs are comparable across teams (perf, infra, product).

Audience
- Perf engineers running lab benchmarks
- Release engineers validating capacity claims
- SRE/infra teams reproducing customer-reported throughput regressions

High-level goals
- Produce median and tail throughput numbers with < 5% run-to-run variance for steady workloads in the lab
- Make warmup and trimming deterministic so CI runs can compare deltas reliably
- Provide actionable checklist items for failed runs and common failure modes

Background and motivation
We observed that identical load scripts produce +/-10–25% throughput variability depending on entropy in inputs, client pacing jitter, GPU microstate (thermal), and model kv-cache behavior. Ad-hoc warmups hide many of these effects but are inconsistent across teams. Canonicalization reduces a large chunk of variance by fixing input fingerprints and arrival scaffolding; seed heuristics ensure deterministic client-side pseudo-random behavior. Temporal stabilization enforces a warmup and measurement window policy that trims initial transient behavior and microbursts.

Canonical workload rules (what to lock down)
- Input set: maintain a small canonical corpus per model family (10–50 prompts) that span sequence length percentiles (P10/P50/P90). Store canonical corpus in bench/artifacts/canonical/<model>.jsonl with SHA256 manifest.
- Deterministic tokenization: include tokenizer version and config in the manifest; bench must abort if tokenizers mismatch.
- Request payload fingerprinting: canonical inputs must be normalized (trim whitespace, normalized punctuation) to avoid pre-tokenization nondeterminism.
- Arrival skeleton: generate arrival times from a seeded process (see RNG section). Do not rely on OS-level nondeterministic sleep() jitter.

Seed hygiene and RNG heuristics
- Single-seed policy: every benchmark run uses a single canonical seed per experiment. Seed is recorded in run metadata and the artifact manifest.
- Seed sources: use reproducible PRNG (xoshiro256**) with explicit seed value. Avoid system-provided rng without explicit seeding.
- Per-client determinism: for multi-client loadgens, derive client seeds via a deterministic function: client_seed = hash(global_seed || client_id). This prevents accidental seed collisions.
- Entropy knobs: when we intentionally want variance (e.g., simulate real traffic), use an explicit seed-schedule file with documented seeds rather than ad-hoc randomness.

Temporal stabilization heuristic (warmup + trimming)
1) Stage A — priming (60–180s): send single-threaded serial requests to populate model caches and GPU memory pages. This is short, focused priming, not full throughput warmup. Is aimed at JITs and driver allocations.
2) Stage B — occupancy ramp (5–15 minutes): ramp to target concurrency using staircase increments (e.g., 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) holding each for 60s. This brings scheduling steady state and warms up batching kernels.
3) Stage C — steady probe (3–10 minutes): hold at target concurrency and collect fine-grained samples (100ms buckets). This period is used to compute rolling-window stability diagnostics.
4) Stage D — measurement window: choose a contiguous measurement window inside Stage C where variance and occupancy show stationarity (see diagnostics below). Typical measurement windows are 180–300s for CI, 600–1800s for release claims.

Measurement and trimming rules
- Rolling median smoothing: compute throughput in 1s and 10s buckets. Reject the first N seconds where throughput < 80% of the max observed during Stage C. N is capped at 30% of Stage C length.
- Stationarity test: perform an augmented Dickey-Fuller style check on the 10s throughput series; if non-stationary, extend Stage C by one interval and re-evaluate.
- Outlier removal: drop top/bottom 5% of 1s buckets when computing mean throughput. Report median and 90th percentile of per-bucket throughput.
- Thermal-aware flagging: correlate GPU temperature trace with throughput; if a rising temperature trend correlates with throughput drop > 5%, mark run as thermally-affected and fail reproducibility gates.

Diagnostics to collect (minimum)
- Per-request: start_ts, end_ts, request_id, input_fingerprint, sequence_length, tokens_out
- Runtime: GPU_util, GPU_mem_total, GPU_mem_used, PCIe_retries, driver_version, cudnn_version
- Client: host_clock_drift, event_loop_lag, process_cpu, per-client_queue_depth
- Loadgen: seed, client_id, arrival_schedule_hash, tokenization_manifest_sha256
- Environmental: room temp (if available), pdu/load, infra deployment tag

Loadgen config snippets (pseudocode)
- arrival schedule:  // YAML-like example
  seed: 123456789
  distribution: poisson
  lambda: 1200
  jitter_policy: disabled
  client_shard: 0..15

- sample input manifest entry:
  id: c10_p90_01
  model_family: redwood-7b
  tokenizer_sha: sha256:abc123
  prompt: "Summarize the following email: {{email_blob}}"

Practical checklists before a run
- Verify canonical corpus manifest SHA matches expected commit
- Lock model binary and runtime kernel table to the versions in run metadata
- Ensure all clients are started with same PRNG implementation and global_seed exported
- Confirm clocks on client machines are NTP-synced to <50ms skew
- Pre-flush node caches if previous unrelated runs elevated memory usage
- Start temperature monitors and baseline them for 2 minutes before Stage A

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Symptom: large early throughput spike then collapse
  Mitigation: extend Stage B ramp, check for batching oversubscription and KV cache thrashing; reduce ramp step sizes.
- Symptom: high variance across runs with identical seeds
  Mitigation: check model binary/kv-cache warm paths, capture driver logs, and replay Stage A priming with verbose tracing.
- Symptom: time-of-day correlated drops
  Mitigation: verify noisy neighbor infra and scheduled maintenance; prefer off-peak lab windows for release runs.

Quick reproducibility gating rules
- CI-level: run length 180s measurement, variance threshold median throughput delta < 7% across 3 consecutive runs with same seed.
- Release-level: run length 900s measurement, variance threshold < 5% across 5 runs, thermal and stationarity checks must pass.

Appendix A — canonical manifest minimal fields
- manifest_version
- model_tag
- tokenizer_sha256
- inputs_count
- input_ids -> list of short labels
- canonical_seed
- owner

Appendix B — minimal telemetry endpoints and retention
- bench should upload metrics to perf-ingest/bench-runs with run_id and artifacts.gz within 24h of completion. Retain artifacts for 90d.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we include a lightweight hardware fingerprint (microcode, BIOS) in the run metadata for long-tail variance debugging? (Proposal: yes for release-level runs)
- Evaluate whether 1s buckets are too noisy for smaller batch sizes; consider 200ms buckets for latency-sensitive models.
- Integrate a simple golden-run replay mode into the loadgen: replay exact arrival timestamps for perfect bitwise repeatability across labs.

Author notes
This is intentionally pragmatic: canonicalization reduces comments/noise in comms and helps triage real regressions faster. The heuristic values (times, thresholds) have been tuned from lab experiments and will be iterated based on further CI experience.

Checklist for publishing a canonical workload (quick):
- [ ] create canonical corpus file and record SHA in manifest
- [ ] add tokenization config and model tag to manifest
- [ ] pick canonical_seed and record in run metadata
- [ ] run the 4-stage stabilization protocol and confirm stationarity
- [ ] upload artifacts and file a perf ticket if variance > threshold

End of notes.
